title: Agenda and Minutes of Meetings and Conferences
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 6
notes: Sample layouts of an agenda and minutes at Annexes A and B to Chapter 6.

rules.title: Agenda subject heading states purpose, location, room, time and date
rules.description: The agenda's subject heading states the general purpose of the meeting, together with the location, room, time and date.
rules.notes: Heuristic: checks the agenda heading covers the four required elements.

rules.title: Agenda items are numbered and each has a heading
rules.description: The items to be discussed must be in a logical order and each item of the agenda is given a number and a heading.

rules.title: Series meetings: first items and last item follow convention
rules.description: When the meeting is one of a series, the first item should be 'Minutes of Last Meeting' followed by 'Matters Arising from Last Meeting' and the last item should be 'Arrangements for Next Meeting'.

rules.title: Any Other Business is included after the last item
rules.description: The item 'Any Other Business' or 'AOB' is normally included after the last item discussion.

rules.title: Minutes record decisions, action required and who takes the action
rules.description: Minutes of a meeting summarize relevant discussions, record decisions taken, state the action required, and specify who is to take the action.
rules.notes: Heuristic: minutes should include an action column or action list with named actionees.

rules.title: Minutes must be impersonal
rules.description: Minutes are written in an impersonal form: 'A said ...', 'B replied ...' must be avoided; individuals are referred to by appointment, and the chairperson is always referred to as 'the chairman'.

rules.title: Minutes must be accurate, brief and logically arranged
rules.description: Minutes must be accurate, brief, logically arranged, impersonal and in appropriate tenses; they are not a verbatim record.
